questions.question: What is a wave in a basic physics description?
choices: A transfer of material that requires every particle to travel the entire route
A force that must act only in a vacuum
A change in the mass of every particle

questions.question: What is wavelength?
choices: The number of cycles occurring each second
The distance between corresponding points on adjacent cycles
The time needed for one complete cycle

questions.question: What is frequency?
choices: The distance a wave travels in one cycle
The number of cycles per unit time

questions.question: What is amplitude?
choices: The wave's frequency divided by speed
The number of waves in a medium

questions.question: Which unit is used for frequency?
What is a transverse wave?
choices: A wave with oscillations perpendicular to its direction of travel
A wave with particles moving only along its travel direction
A wave that cannot be reflected

questions.question: Sound in air is mainly which type of wave?
Why does sound not travel through an ideal vacuum?
choices: A vacuum absorbs every frequency equally
Sound can travel only through solids

questions.question: How does higher sound frequency generally affect perceived pitch?
choices: It changes only the source's mass
It makes pitch independent of the wave

questions.question: How does greater sound-wave amplitude generally affect loudness under otherwise similar conditions?
choices: It is associated with greater intensity and usually greater loudness
It guarantees a change in wavelength
It removes the need for a medium

questions.question: What happens during reflection of a wave?
choices: The wave returns from a boundary into its original medium
The wave changes into a different kind of matter
The wave must stop moving permanently
The wave loses all its energy instantly

questions.question: What is an echo?
choices: A sound produced only inside solids
A reflected sound heard after the original
A sound that has no material source

questions.question: What happens to wavelength if frequency increases while wave speed remains constant?
choices: Wavelength increases at the same rate

questions.question: Why can a floating object bob as a water wave passes without traveling across the pond?
choices: All waves require permanent bulk transport of the medium
The disturbance transfers energy while local material mainly oscillates

questions.question: How can a wave change direction when entering a region where its speed changes?
choices: Refraction can alter its travel direction

questions.question: A wave has frequency 2 Hz and wavelength 3 m. Using v = fλ, what is its speed?
A wave completes 10 cycles in 5 s. What is its frequency?
Two sounds have equal amplitude but different frequencies. Which difference is most directly expected?
choices: Different travel speeds in the same air necessarily
Different directions of particle oscillation necessarily

questions.question: In air, a listener hears a siren at a higher pitch as its source approaches. Which effect explains this?
choices: A decrease in the source's emitted frequency

questions.question: An astronaut watches an explosion across empty space. Why would its sound not arrive through that empty space?
choices: There is no material medium to transmit the sound
Light requires air but sound does not
